text: Which statement is the Compactness Theorem for first-order logic?
choices: A theory is complete if and only if it is consistent
Every satisfiable theory has a finite model
A theory has a model if and only if it is finite
A set Γ of sentences is satisfiable if and only if every finite subset of Γ is satisfiable
explanation: Compactness states Γ is satisfiable iff every finite subset of Γ is satisfiable. Option B is false (satisfiable theories can force infinite models, e.g. non-standard arithmetic); option C conflates having a model with being finite; option A confuses completeness with consistency. Only D is the theorem.
